newsitem.title: UK: Russia's Ingosstrakh says ready to expand abroad.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Ingosstrakh says ready to expand abroad.

text.p: Russia's largest insurer Ingosstrakh is considering insuring its first risks outside its home market of the CIS and Baltic states, company president Vladimir Krouglyak told a conference on Friday.

"Our potential is enough to enter the European market, to make a few cautious steps in this direction and take on a few risks," he said at a conference entitled "Realities of financial stabilisation in Russia - the return of Russian insurance to the world market".

Until now, Ingosstrakh has restricted itself to insuring risks in its home markets and to obtaining reinsurance, primarily in the London Market, he told the conference of Russian and London based insurers.
In a 15 year business development programme unveiled in August, the company said it aimed to become one of the leading providers of insurance services on the international market.

Ingosstrakh has long had links with the London insurance market, which Krouglyak said was the world's unofficial insurance capital, through its subsidiary Black Sea and Baltic General Insurance Co Ltd.
Black Sea and Baltic has operated in London since 1925 and specialises in insuring business between Russia and the rest of the world.

Krouglyak said Russian insurers faced two major difficulties -- the deplorable state of the Russian economy and the lack of a legislative framework to manage relationships between the state, insurers and insured.

However, the government was aware of the importance of insurance in developing the economy, a fact that was reinforced by foreign capital providers insisting that projects in Russia be insured, he added.

Ingosstrakh's preliminary results for the first half of 1996 showed premium income of 375.5 billion roubles compared with claims of 134.2 billion. At July 30, the company had gross assets of 2,220 billion roubles.
